title: The Foundation
idea: Wealth is created, not taken. When your thought, your daily action and your dealings with people line up, you stop competing and start creating.
do: Write your clear mental image on one page: what you want, specifically, as if it is complete.
Make today a success: list today's tasks and finish each one as well as you can.
In every exchange today, give more in use-value than you take in cash-value.
Notice one moment of hurry and slow down on purpose.
say: I operate entirely upon the creative plane.
I give more in use-value than I receive in cash-value.
I advance the life of every person I touch.
remember: Rise from the competitive plane to the creative plane.
Every day is a success or a failure. Make today a success.
Never hurry.
reflect: Where am I competing when I could be creating?
What would "more use-value" look like in my work this week?
Describe my completed picture in three sentences.
track: Read the daily affirmation each morning

title: Choosing Abundance
idea: Abundance is a lens you choose. Attention is light: what you focus on grows. Gratitude is the bridge from feeling lack to feeling abundant, even before the facts change.
do: Catch one scarcity thought today. Name it, then choose the abundance lens.
Name three things you already have.
Give thanks in advance for one thing that is on its way.
In a hard moment: notice, name it honestly, then give thanks.
say: There is enough, and more can be created.
Today is one frame, not the whole film.
Thank you for what is already on its way.
remember: The lens is a choice.
Abundance is not denial. Hard seasons are real, and so is the open window.
Feeling abundant does not wait for more.
reflect: Three things I already have:
One thing I am grateful for in advance:
A hard-season thought I can see through a new lens:

title: The Clear Vision
idea: A vague wish stays a wish. Know exactly what you want, write it down, and hold the completed picture with gratitude.
do: Write one page describing your completed vision, in the present tense.
Make it specific: what it buys, what it builds, and who you become.
Read it once in the morning and once at night.
When an obstacle grabs your attention, return your light to the vision.
say: I see it clearly.
Thank you. It is already on its way.
My attention feeds my vision.
remember: You cannot move toward a blur.
Attention feeds what it touches.
Clarity plus gratitude becomes faith.
reflect: My completed vision, in one sentence:
Where I am, who is with me, how it feels:
The obstacle I will stop feeding:

title: Release the Contest
idea: Comparison turns life into a race with no finish line. Step off the track onto the open field, where value is created and there is room for everyone.
do: Notice one comparison today.
Name it gently, without judgment.
Bless that person silently and sincerely.
Create one small thing today instead of competing.
say: There is room for all of us.
Their light is welcome.
I create my own.
remember: Attention spent on their lane is light taken from your own.
Their success is proof of what is possible, not a threat.
Make more. Don't take more.
reflect: Who do I compare myself to most, and what does their success show is possible?
Where can I create this week instead of compete?
How did my own light change when I blessed them?
track: Notice, name, bless — once a day

title: The Daily Work
idea: Thought becomes real through action: one complete day at a time, one task at a time, with your full attention.
do: Morning: choose three things for today. Just three.
Midday: one thing at a time, fully.
Evening: close the day with three things completed and one thank-you.
Leave one interaction better than you found it.
say: Today is complete in itself.
Not more effort. More presence.
I do my part, and I trust the soil.
remember: Judge the accumulation of days, not one day.
Hurry splits attention. Calm gathers it.
Nothing is small when it is done with purpose.
reflect: My three things today:
What I completed:
My one thank-you:

title: Give First
idea: Abundance moves through you. Give more in use-value than you take in cash-value, from overflow, and with no string attached.
do: Choose one gift for today: attention, kindness, skill, time or resources.
Before one task, ask: how can I be more useful here?
Fill your own cup first by naming three things you are grateful for.
Give one gift with no string attached.
say: I have enough to give.
I give freely.
How can I be more useful today?
remember: A pond that only takes grows still. A spring that gives stays fresh.
Healthy giving keeps its boundaries.
Value that circulates tends to return, often from places you did not expect.
reflect: Attention I can give:
Kindness I can give:
Skill I can give:
Time I can give:
Resources I can give:

title: Unhurried
idea: Hurry is scarcity wearing a watch. Move with calm assurance and act in faith: do your part completely, and trust the process.
do: When you notice rushing, take one slow breath before acting.
Do one task today at half speed with full attention.
Take only the next visible step on a big goal. The road appears as you walk it.
Name your part, and name what you can leave to time.
say: I am unhurried.
Everything is moving.
I do my part. I trust the process.
remember: Nature never hurries, and yet everything is accomplished.
Calm is not slow. Calm is clear.
Faith is not passive. Stay awake to what is real.
reflect: Where does hurry show up in my body?
What is the next step my lantern shows me?
What is my part, and what can I let the wind do?

title: The Morning Practice
idea: How you begin shapes how you move. Five minutes, seven movements, one for each step, every morning.
do: Lens: say "there is enough, and more can be created."
Picture: hold your completed vision for three slow breaths.
Gratitude: name three things, then one more in advance.
Contest: bless one person you might compare yourself to.
Work: choose three things for today.
Give: choose one gift for today.
Unhurried: slow your breath and trust the process.
say: I choose abundance.
My vision is clear. My gratitude is constant.
I release the contest. I give first. I move unhurried.
There is enough. There is more to create. I begin.
remember: Before the world asks anything of you, arrive.
Five minutes is enough.
Begin with gratitude.
reflect: My three things today:
My one gift today:
The person I bless today:
